title: Strain engineering of transient exciton diffusion in WSe2 monolayers at cryogenic temperatures
authors: Roberto Rosati, Mohammed Adel Aly Nouh, Robert Schmidt, Rudolf Bratschitsch, Ermin Malic
abstract: Tungsten-based transition metal dichalcogenides exhibit dark excitons as the energetically lowest states. These are crucial for exciton thermalization and propagation and they dominate low-temperature photoluminescence via the emergence of pronounced phonon sidebands. After a resonant excitation, highly mobile hot dark excitons are formed, which quickly thermalize into an equilibrium distribution. The application of strain modifies the exciton energy landscape and, in particular, the relative energy separation between bright and dark exciton states. The impact of strain on the transient photoluminescence and diffusion of non-equilibrium excitons has remained largely unexplored so far. In this work, we investigate the spatiotemporal exciton dynamics in strained hBN-encapsulated WSe2 monolayers at cryogenic temperatures. We demonstrate that tensile strain abruptly increases the excess energy of hot excitons, thereby accelerating their transient diffusion. We trace this back to suppressed phonon-mediated scattering from bright to dark excitons. Furthermore, we predict a periodic modulation of the transient exciton diffusion in the presence of a compressive strain resulting from strain-driven emission of M phonons. The gained microscopic insights illustrate how strain can be used to engineer transient photoluminescence and exciton diffusion in technologically promising 2D semiconductors.
summary: This research demonstrates that strain engineering offers a powerful tool to control exciton dynamics in WSe2 monolayers. By applying tensile or compressive strain, researchers can modify the energy landscape and suppress specific phonon scattering channels. This manipulation results in an abrupt enhancement of hot dark exciton excess energy and significantly accelerates transient exciton diffusion, paving the way for tailored 2D semiconductor devices.
main_problem: The study investigates how strain engineering can precisely control the transient exciton diffusion and energy landscape within WSe2 monolayers at cryogenic temperatures.
main_result: Tensile strain above a critical threshold ($s > s_0$) abruptly increases hot dark exciton excess energy, leading to an accelerated transient diffusion coefficient. Compressive strain is predicted to induce periodic modulation of this diffusion via M-phonon emission.
method: The work combines theoretical modeling using master equations for excitonic dynamics with experimental measurements of time- and energy-resolved photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy under controlled uniaxial strain.
model_or_system: The physical system is WSe2 monolayers encapsulated by hBN, focusing on the interplay between bright and dark exciton states. The dynamics are modeled using an excitonic intravalley Wigner function governed by a master equation that includes spatial evolution, radiative losses, and strain-dependent exciton-phonon scattering terms.
key_observables: Transient PL spectrum ($I_s(E, \mathbf{r}, t)$), effective diffusion coefficient $D_s(t)$, and the excess energy of hot excitons ($\langle E_s angle_t$).
important_parameters: Strain magnitude ($s$), critical strain threshold ($s_0 \approx 0.3\%$), cryogenic temperatures (20 K, 50 K), and phonon energies (M phonons).
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on the lowest 1s states of specific exciton complexes ($	ext{KK}$, $	ext{K}\Lambda$, $	ext{KK}'$) and uses a Markov approach for scattering dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how tensile strain causes spectral reordering, leading to faster transport by deactivating certain scattering channels; another figure shows the abrupt enhancement of $D_s(t)$ above $s_0$ with temperature dependence.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the effect of strain on exciton energy levels (via Wannier equations), models the resulting changes in scattering rates using a master equation, and quantifies the impact on measurable observables like PL spectra shifts and diffusion coefficients ($D_s(t)$).
why_interesting: This work provides quantitative rules for manipulating quantum transport properties (exciton diffusion) in 2D materials by external mechanical fields (strain), which is highly relevant to designing next-generation optoelectronic devices.
